evidence.note: 1H 9.57 and 13C 185.0 indicate a CHO conjugated with an electron-rich aryl ring; 185 is low for an aryl aldehyde.
Three ArH and six aromatic carbons (one C-N at 151.3) fit a trisubstituted benzene.
N-CH2 signals at 3.37/3.29 ppm and 56.0/44.6 ppm fit an N-ethyl indoline nitrogen.
1.20 ppm and 17.2 ppm fit the CH3 of an N-ethyl group.

candidates.name: 1-ethylindoline-5-carbaldehyde
candidates.rationale: DoU 6 = benzene (4) + CHO (1) + indoline ring (1). The sp3 pattern fits N-ethylindoline: ring NCH2 at 3.37 (56.0), NCH2CH3 at 3.29 (44.6), benzylic C3H2 at 3.14 (29.3) and CH3 at 1.20 (17.2). The CHO (9.57, 185.0) sits para to N. Shielded H7 at 6.08 lies ortho to N; 151.3 is C7a. The C=O at 185 is low for an aryl aldehyde.

candidates.name: 1-ethylindoline-6-carbaldehyde
candidates.rationale: Same N-ethylindoline sp3 pattern (peaks 5-8, 16-19) with CHO meta to N. This places the shielded 6.08 proton less well, since H7 would sit between N and CHO.

candidates.name: 1-methyl-1,2,3,4-tetrahydroquinoline-6-carbaldehyde
candidates.rationale: Isomeric aminobenzaldehyde with matching DoU. However, 1.20/17.2 fits a ring CH2 poorly, and NCH3 would appear near 2.9-3.0 ppm, so it is less consistent.

first.reasoning_summary: C11H13NO has DoU 6. 13C shows one C=O at 185.0 with the 1H signal at 9.57, consistent with a conjugated aldehyde, plus six aromatic carbons (151.3 is C-N) and three ArH (8.25, 6.98, 6.08). That accounts for benzene + CHO = 5 DoU, leaving one ring. The four sp3 carbons (56.0, 44.6, 29.3, 17.2) and protons at 3.37, 3.29, 3.14 and 1.20 match an N-ethylindoline: ring NCH2, NCH2CH3, benzylic CH2 and CH3. The proton sum is 1+3+2+2+2+3 = 13. The para-amino aldehyde (5-CHO) best explains the shielded 6.08 ArH ortho to N. The 185 ppm carbonyl is somewhat low for this assignment, which limits confidence in the ranking.

evidence.note: 185.0 ppm lies in the ketone range but below the aldehyde window, consistent with an aryl ketone conjugated with an amine.
Six sp2 carbons, including a C-N carbon at 151.3, plus several ArH signals.
The N-CH2 signal at 3.37 ppm and 56.0 ppm fits an N-aryl tertiary amine.
1.20 and 17.2 ppm fit a CH3 on a CH.

candidates.name: 1-ethyl-2,3-dihydroquinolin-4(1H)-one
candidates.rationale: Same scaffold with N-ethyl. NCH2 signals at 3.37/3.29 (5,6), CH2C=O at 3.14 (7), CH3 at 1.20 (8). The ketone is 185.0 (9) and C-N aromatic carbon 151.3 (10).

candidates.name: 2,3-dimethyl-2,3-dihydroquinolin-4(1H)-one
candidates.rationale: Secondary-amine isomer that assigns 9.57 to NH, with CH-N 56.0 (16) and CH alpha to C=O 44.6 (17). One methyl would need to sit at 29.3 (18), which is a poor fit.

repaired.reasoning_summary: The carbonyl at 185.0 falls outside the aldehyde window, so it is treated as a conjugated ketone. With a benzene ring (151.3 C-N) and DoU 6, a 2,3-dihydroquinolin-4-one scaffold fits. 1H at 3.37/3.29/3.14 and 1.20 with 13C at 56.0/44.6/29.3/17.2 suit an N-CH2, a CH alpha to C=O, an NCH3 and a CHCH3. Peak 3 (6.98) is assigned 2H to reach H = 13, which is an assumption because the table gives no integrals. In rank 1, NCH3 at 29.3 is low (expected near 38-39), and peak 1 (9.57) is unexplained. Ranks 2 and 3 are alternative isomers with weaker fits.
